name: Foundation Models
oneLiner: Large neural networks trained on broad data that can be adapted to many tasks.

analogy.text: A widely read apprentice: has absorbed a huge library and can attempt almost anything, but needs direction to be useful.
analogy.breaks: An apprentice remembers what they read. A model stores statistical patterns, not a searchable library, so it can produce fluent text that is simply wrong.

givesAbove: A general capability, predicting and generating text and other media, packaged as model weights.
needsBelow: Training data from Data and large clusters from Cloud & Infrastructure.

walkthrough.title: Text becomes tokens
walkthrough.text: “The cat sat on the” is snapped into tokens, and each token becomes a vector of numbers.

walkthrough.title: Attention mixes in context
walkthrough.text: Layer after layer, each token looks back at the earlier ones, so “the” knows a cat is sitting.

walkthrough.title: One token is predicted
walkthrough.text: The last layer scores every possible next token; “mat” gets the highest probability, and one token is picked.

walkthrough.title: Pretraining set the weights
walkthrough.text: All of that only works because pretraining tuned billions of weights by predicting the next token across trillions of examples.

walkthrough.title: Post-training makes it an assistant, then it's released
walkthrough.text: Fine-tuning and feedback turn the predictor into a helpful assistant, released either as open weights or behind an API.
